claim: AGoQ reduces GPU memory by up to 52% and improves training speed by up to 1.34x versus Megatron-LM (with/without ZeRO), DeepSpeed and COAT on 8B-32B LLaMA models.
stance_target: activation+gradient quantisation is a viable memory-efficiency lever
quoted_support: the experimental results show that our AGoQ reduces the memory by up to 52% and achieves up to 1.34× improvement of training speed compared to state-of-the-art training systems Megatron-LM (w/ or w/o ZeRO), COAT and DeepSpeed with 8B to 32B LLaMA models

claim: Near-4-bit activation storage cuts activation memory from 28U in Megatron-LM to 7.75U - an approximately three-fold reduction (RMSNorm 4U->0.5U, SiLU&Multiply 12U->2U, attention 5U).
stance_target: layer-aware activation quantisation substantially cuts activation memory
quoted_support: Overall, activation memory drops from 28U in Megatron-LM to 7.75U in our method—an approximate three-fold reduction.

claim: Gradient memory drops 75% versus COAT and activation memory a further 30%, by storing gradients in 8-bit for local accumulation.
stance_target: 8-bit gradient storage is a large memory lever
quoted_support: compared to COAT, we reduce activation memory by an additional 30% and gradient memory by 75%

claim: The 8-bit All-Reduce is decomposed into quantise -> reduce-scatter -> re-quantise -> all-gather so the reduction happens in high precision while the wire payload stays 8-bit.
quoted_support: After local accumulation, GPUs perform a precision-preserved FP8 All-Reduce across GPUs

claim: On a simulated 10 Gbps commodity link, the decomposed 8-bit all-reduce is 3.7x faster than the baseline at a 32 MB message (432.36 ms vs 1,603.78 ms).
stance_target: 8-bit collectives pay off MORE on low-bandwidth fabrics
scope_conditions: TP=8, DP=8, 32 MB message, 10 Gbps simulated
quoted_support: Under 10Gbps, the speedup increases to 3.7× (432.36 ms vs 1603.78 ms), confirming that our method delivers substantial communication savings across diverse bandwidth settings.

claim: At 200 Gbps the same comparison yields 3.4x (39.17 ms vs 131.23 ms) - a smaller relative gain than at 10 Gbps.
stance_target: compression/quantisation benefit grows as bandwidth falls
quoted_support: At 32MB under 200Gbps, our decomposed approach achieves a 3.4× speedup (39.17 ms vs. 131.23 ms).

claim: The primary testbed is 64x RTX A6000 over 200 Gb/s InfiniBand, and the FP8 comparison required NVIDIA Pro 6000 GPUs 'to support the FP8 format required by COAT'.
stance_target: hardware requirements for FP8 training paths
quoted_support: Experiments are mainly carried out on a 64-GPU cluster connected with 200Gb/s InfiniBand comprising 8 nodes, each of which is equipped with eight Nvidia A6000 GPUs. In the comparative experiments with COAT (Xi et al., 2025), we used two nodes, each equipped with 8 NVIDIA Pro 6000 GPUs, to support the FP8 format required by COAT.

claim: FP8 requires sm_89+/Hopper-class hardware; GA100 (sm_80) has no native FP8, so an 8-bit path on a CMP 170HX would need int8 or emulated FP8, which this paper does not measure.
stance_target: AGoQ's FP8 results transfer directly to Ampere-generation mining cards
quoted_support: we used two nodes, each equipped with 8 NVIDIA Pro 6000 GPUs, to support the FP8 format required by COAT

claim: AGoQ preserves convergence loss on pretraining and comparable downstream accuracy on LLaMA architectures despite 4-bit activations and 8-bit gradients.
stance_target: aggressive activation/gradient quantisation can be quality-neutral
quoted_support: while achieving convergence loss on pretraining and comparable accuracy on downstream tasks with LLaMA architectures

claim: AGoQ also supports Huawei Ascend 910 NPUs, indicating the technique is not tied to NVIDIA-specific collective libraries.
quoted_support: Our system also supports Huawei Ascend 910 NPUs (more results can be found in Appendix 8.2).

claim: The 10 Gbps experiment is the closest published analogue to the CMP box's ~0.75 GiB/s (~6 Gbps) NCCL fabric, and it shows the relative win from halving payload grows as bandwidth falls.
stance_target: 8-bit gradient collectives are a strong lever on a Gen2 x4 PCIe fabric
scope_conditions: 10 Gbps simulated vs 0.75 GiB/s measured on CMP 170HX
quoted_support: We evaluated communication efficiency under two representative bandwidth conditions: 200Gbps (our primary testbed) and 10Gbps (to simulate commodity constraints).

claim: Quantisation/dequantisation in AGoQ is fused into GEMM kernels, so the compute overhead of the 8-bit path is largely hidden rather than added to step time.
stance_target: 8-bit collectives need not add measurable compute overhead
quoted_support: Quantization/dequantization are fused into GEMM kernels.
